questions.question: Should you always drive more slowly than other traffic?

options.text: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
Yes, it is good defensive driving.
Yes, it is always safer than driving faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly in heavy traffic or bad weather. But if you drive too slowly and block the normal flow of traffic, you can get a ticket.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car directly in front of you.
Keep your eyes moving to spot possible hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your eyes moving to spot possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means scanning ahead for hazards. Do not stare only at the road in front of your car. Look ahead and stay alert to vehicles around you.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is safe.
Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
Speed does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can be dangerous. Drivers behind you may get frustrated and make risky moves to pass you. It is safest to drive with the traffic flow and within the speed limit.

questions.question: Where should a 12-year-old sit in a car with airbags?

options.text: The front seat
The back seat
Any seat

questions.correctAnswerText: The back seat
questions.explanation: A child should not sit in the front passenger seat, especially if there is an airbag. An airbag can seriously injure a child. State law requires all children under 14 to sit in the rear seat with proper safety restraints.

questions.question: If you need to use your cell phone while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep phone calls short.
Stop in a safe parking area before using your phone.
Use a hands-free device and keep both hands on the wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop in a safe parking area before using your phone.
questions.explanation: Stop in a safe parking area before using your cell phone. Any distraction while driving is dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign shows a crosswalk may be ahead. Be alert and let pedestrians cross safely.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line down the center of a road mean?

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on a two-lane road means any driver may pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must drive through the intersection at this speed.
The maximum speed limit is 55 mph under ideal conditions.
You must not drive slower than this speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed limit is 55 mph under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum speed limit for this road. You can drive slower based on road conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: In which situation should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to turn left at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
When parked on the side of a level road with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
questions.explanation: Keep your wheels straight when waiting to turn left. This prevents you from sliding into oncoming traffic if hit from behind. On a hill or slope, turn your wheels so your car will not roll into traffic if brakes fail.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: The same as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
The same as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely. Yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe. This is the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: Yellow lines separate:

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of roads with traffic moving both ways. A solid yellow line means you cannot cross it to pass. A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass if it is safe.

questions.question: To avoid losing traction on wet roads, you should:

options.text: Make abrupt turns.
Apply the brakes firmly.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on wet roads to prevent hydroplaning and keep your tires in good condition. If you lose control, release the gas pedal, do not brake, keep the vehicle straight, and let it slow down naturally.

questions.question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means that vehicles:

options.text: Driving in both directions may pass.
Next to the broken line may pass.
Next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. If you are next to a broken yellow line, you may pass.

questions.question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:

options.text: Ease up on the gas pedal.
Brake as hard as possible.
Turn off the ignition.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease up on the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, release the gas pedal or brakes to regain balance. Steer in the direction of the skid to get control of the vehicle again.

questions.question: Check your rearview mirrors:

options.text: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
questions.explanation: While driving, check your rearview mirrors regularly. This helps you know where vehicles are near you at all times.

questions.question: If you are driving at night and a vehicle is approaching with its high beam headlights on:

options.text: Quickly flash your headlights one time.
Do not dim your high beam headlights.
Look in the direction of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Quickly flash your headlights one time.
questions.explanation: Flash your headlights one time to signal the other driver to dim their lights. If they do not, look toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded. Do not use your own high beams in response.

questions.question: If a traffic signal light is green and a police officer signals for you to stop, you should:

options.text: Obey the officer.
Obey the traffic signal.
Do what the vehicle in front of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey the officer.
questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's directions, even if they conflict with traffic signs, signals, or road markings.

questions.question: When preparing to make a left turn from a two-way street, you should drive:

options.text: Near the right-hand side of the road.
Near the centerline.
On the left of the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the centerline.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street, drive in the lane closest to the centerline. Start your turn just before your car reaches the center of the intersection. Turn into the first available legal lane without cutting the corner.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or carrying a white cane:

options.text: The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.
You must yield the right-of-way.
Honk your horn to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind pedestrians use a white cane or guide dog. You must yield the right-of-way to these pedestrians.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Flagger ahead.
Turn left at the intersection.
Last turn before a toll road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flagger ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barrels mark work zones. This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead. Follow the flagger's directions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School zone or crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone or crossing.
questions.explanation: A yellow or yellow-green five-sided sign warns drivers about a school zone or school crossing.

questions.question: A large truck is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. What might the truck do?

options.text: May complete its turn in either of the two lanes.
May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns, the rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks need extra space to turn. They often swing wide to complete a right turn.

questions.question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: There isn't room on the other side for you to completely cross the tracks.
The railroad crossing is located in a city or town that has frequent train traffic.
You are transporting two or more young children in a passenger vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: There isn't room on the other side for you to completely cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: A train can come on any track at any time. Before crossing the tracks, make sure your vehicle has room to completely clear them. Never stop your vehicle on the tracks.

questions.question: When used on roadways, what are bicycles considered?

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles when used on roadways. Bicyclists and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No turns are allowed on the road.
The road narrows ahead.
There is a series of curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a series of curves ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions coming up ahead. This sign warns drivers that the road will curve.
